# Ibd

This folder contains the specific clinical quality indicators used by the Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease (DANIBD) registry to monitor and evaluate the standard of care for IBD patients across Denmark. The indicators track a wide range of clinical and operational metrics, including the timeliness and completeness of diagnostic workups for both adults and children, post-operative follow-ups for Crohn's disease, patient education rates, and the systematic monitoring of patients on biological therapies or those requiring surgery. Together, these pages detail the national and regional fulfillment rates, development targets, and local hospital audits that highlight both the systemic successes and the data-capture challenges inherent in managing a national clinical quality database.

## Pages

- [[indikator-1]] — Measures the overall quality of patient investigations, though currently criticized by some hospitals for skewed data capture regarding prior external investigations and patient refusals.
- [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]] — Tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed adult IBD patients who receive a colonoscopy within 12 months of their first hospital contact.
- [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] — Evaluates the diagnostic workup standards for newly diagnosed children and youth, requiring a gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and MRI or capsule endoscopy within a 12-month window.
- [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] — Monitors the proportion of newly diagnosed IBD patients who receive structured patient education within one year of their diagnosis.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Measures the proportion of adult Crohn's disease patients who undergo a follow-up colonoscopy within one year after an ileocecal resection.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Tracks the systematic follow-up of IBD patients on biological and targeted synthetic therapies via annual fecal calprotectin measurements, with some regional redefinition regarding DEXA scans for older patients on steroids.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Monitors the frequency of fecal calprotectin measurements in IBD patients treated with biological and targeted synthetic drugs (BMSL), tracking a substantial national cohort of both children and adults.
- [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] — Measures the rate of re-operations occurring within 30 days of primary IBD surgical interventions, serving as a proxy for surgical quality despite some local criticism of its clinical validity.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Tracks the proportion of adult patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) who receive a follow-up colonoscopy within 18 months.
